title: MIBK Binary VLE/LLE Activity-Model Parameter Fits
description: Combined parameter archive for H2O/MIBK, acrylic-acid/MIBK, and propionic-acid/MIBK systems. H2O/MIBK retains its multi-term temperature-dependent VLE/LLE fit; acid/MIBK recommended parameters use B/T-only interaction forms with VDM vapor association.

source_paper.citation: Rawat, B. S.; Krishna, Shri. Isobaric Vapor-Liquid Equilibria for the Partially Miscible System of Water-Methyl Isobutyl Ketone. Journal of Chemical and Engineering Data 1984, 29, 403-406.

experimental_content_used.homogeneous_Txy: Table I: 14 experimentally measured homogeneous VLE points
experimental_content_used.excluded_Txy_points: Five starred points inside the two-liquid region were excluded because the paper states they were arbitrarily inserted for continuity/correlation purposes.
experimental_content_used.mutual_solubility: Table III: all 18 mutual-solubility points, including literature low-temperature points and the authors' higher-temperature measurements.

fitting_strategy.objective: Simultaneous regression of homogeneous VLE and liquid-liquid mutual solubility, with the reported heteroazeotropic VLLE point given very high weight.

mutual_solubility.residual_basis: relative/log-style solubility error so dilute branches remain influential

VLLE.relaxation_probe: A lighter VLLE weighting improved homogeneous VLE and the aqueous solubility branch somewhat, but worsened the organic-rich solubility branch. No useful Pareto improvement was found while retaining VLLE performance at least as good as the Aspen UNIQUAC set, so the heavily anchored strategy was retained.

fitting_strategy.temperature_dependence_test: A linear c*T term was retained where allowed because it materially improved the combined VLE/LLE regression.

UNIQUAC.status: Recommended UNIQUAC fit for the H2O/MIBK binary when retaining UNIQUAC-VDM in the process model.

comparison.note: The retained custom UNIQUAC fit improves all four aggregate metrics versus the tested Aspen UNIQUAC parameter set while remaining strongly anchored to the heteroazeotrope.

NRTL.status: Recommended NRTL fit if NRTL is used for this binary; it gives the best overall fit of the two tested activity-coefficient models.
NRTL.temperature_dependence_note: Removing the c*T terms degraded the mutual-solubility fit substantially, so both c*T terms are retained.

selection_guidance.UNIQUAC: Use when the surrounding process thermo is UNIQUAC-VDM and model consistency matters.
selection_guidance.NRTL: Use when an isolated H2O/MIBK NRTL scope is acceptable; this regression fits the measured binary data substantially better overall.

source_paper.citation: Linek, J.; Wichterle, I. Liquid-vapour equilibrium LIX. The systems diisopropyl ether-acrylic acid, isopropyl acetate-acrylic acid, acrylic acid-2-ethylhexanol and methyl isobutyl ketone-acrylic acid. Collection of Czechoslovak Chemical Communications 1973, 38, 1846-1852.

MIBK.note: MIBK vapor pressure was taken from the source/validated Antoine treatment used for the VLE regression.

fitting_strategy.reason: Only one isobaric dataset is available, so a flexible multi-term temperature correlation is not identifiable. The B/T form was selected because it has the same parameter count as the previous constant-interaction fit while mapping naturally to a constant interaction-energy interpretation.
fitting_strategy.data_used: all 12 reported binary Txy points at 200 Torr
fitting_strategy.vapor_phase: PFDSim VDM association correction with ideal physical fugacity
fitting_strategy.primary_regression_objective: same VDM-reduced activity-coefficient objective used for the previous constant-parameter comparison, so the B/T and constant fits are directly comparable

B_over_T_probe.UNIQUAC_result: B/T lowers RMS ln(gamma) error and substantially improves vapor-composition prediction, while bubble-temperature MAE increases modestly.
B_over_T_probe.NRTL_result: B/T improves vapor-composition prediction but worsens bubble-temperature MAE.

direct_Txy_alternative_not_selected.description: A separately weighted direct-Txy UNIQUAC regression gave approximately B12=171.65 K and B21=-265.64 K with bubble-temperature MAE about 0.137 C and vapor y_AA MAE about 0.02235. It was not selected here because it uses a different regression objective and is therefore not an apples-to-apples replacement for the archived fit.

UNIQUAC.status: recommended B/T-only UNIQUAC fit for UNIQUAC-VDM process calculations; preferred over the previous constant-ln(tau) form for its energy interpretation and improved underlying activity/vapor-composition fit

comparison_to_previous_constant_ln_tau_f.summary: B/T improves RMS ln(gamma) error by about 6% and vapor y_AA MAE by about 34%, at the cost of about 0.18 C additional bubble-temperature MAE.

NRTL.status: B/T-only NRTL alternative; retained as a validated secondary fit, while UNIQUAC is preferred in the current UNIQUAC-VDM flowsheet

alpha.reason: Fitting alpha from a single isobar is poorly identifiable and produced strong parameter covariance.

comparison_to_previous_constant_tau_fit.summary: B/T improves vapor y_AA MAE but worsens bubble-temperature MAE; therefore it is kept as an alternative rather than the primary recommendation.

systems.selection_guidance: Use the B/T-only UNIQUAC set in the present UNIQUAC-VDM distillation flowsheet. It gives a more natural constant-interaction-energy parameterization and markedly better vapor-composition prediction than the previous constant-ln(tau) fit, although the constant-ln(tau) fit remains better for bubble temperature alone.

source_paper.citation: Wisniak, J.; Tamir, A. Association Effects in Propionic Acid Systems. Journal of Chemical & Engineering Data 1976, 21, 88-90.

experimental_dataset.note: The source paper reports 20 PA/MIBK Txy points at 760 mmHg and explicitly shows that propionic-acid vapor association must be included for thermodynamic consistency.

vapor_association.consistency_note: The supplied PFDSim propionic-acid association constants closely reproduce the association treatment required by the source paper over the experimental temperature range.

MIBK.note: A source/validated MIBK Antoine correlation was used over the full PA/MIBK experimental range; the public NIST correlation was not extrapolated beyond its stated upper-temperature limit.

fitting_strategy.reason: Only one isobaric dataset is available, so flexible temperature dependence is not justified. B/T has the same parameter count as the previous constant-interaction fit and corresponds naturally to a constant interaction-energy form.
fitting_strategy.data_used: all 20 reported binary Txy points at 760 mmHg from the clean publisher Table IV
fitting_strategy.vapor_phase: PFDSim VDM association correction with ideal physical fugacity
fitting_strategy.objective: same VDM-reduced activity-coefficient regression objective used for the previous constant-parameter fit, followed by full bubble-point validation against T and y
fitting_strategy.data_handling_note: The clean ACS Table IV was used directly. The earlier OCR/transcription ambiguity is no longer relevant.
fitting_strategy.B_over_T_result: For PA/MIBK, B/T gives a small but consistent improvement over the constant form in RMS ln(gamma), bubble temperature, and vapor composition for both UNIQUAC and NRTL.

UNIQUAC.status: recommended B/T-only UNIQUAC fit for UNIQUAC-VDM process calculations

comparison_to_previous_constant_ln_tau_f.summary: B/T improves every tracked aggregate metric while retaining the same number of adjustable directional interaction parameters.

NRTL.status: recommended B/T-only NRTL equivalent when an NRTL scope is preferred

alpha.reason: Fitting alpha from a single isobar is poorly identifiable and does not provide a meaningful improvement.

comparison_to_previous_constant_tau_fit.summary: B/T gives a small, consistent improvement in every tracked aggregate metric.

systems.selection_guidance: Use the B/T-only UNIQUAC set in the current UNIQUAC-VDM flowsheet. For PA/MIBK the B/T form is preferred without qualification: it is slightly better statistically than the constant form, has the same parameter count, and has a clearer constant-interaction-energy interpretation.

VDM_implementation.description: PFDSim Vapor Dimerization Model with ideal physical fugacity
VDM_implementation.fugacity_decomposition: ln(phi_i) = ln(phi_i^P) + ln(phi_i^D), with phi_i^P = 1 for these regressions

common_model_notes.parameter_recommendation: For the current flowsheet, use the B/T-only UNIQUAC fits for both AA/MIBK and PA/MIBK. PA/MIBK improves cleanly versus the constant form. AA/MIBK trades a modest increase in bubble-temperature error for substantially better vapor-composition and ln(gamma) fit, while gaining a more natural interaction-energy interpretation. Keep the NRTL B/T fits as validated alternatives for isolated NRTL scopes.
common_model_notes.why_no_LLE_data: Ternary LLE regressions were intentionally excluded because effective LLE binary parameters can absorb ternary behavior and are not necessarily transferable to VLE/distillation.
